dedupe_keys.name: zindi and itu green telecom data base station site energy use solar output grid outage plans diesel and battery configuration

description: The Smart Energy Supply Scheduling for Green Telecom Challenge (August to September 2024) was run on Zindi with the ITU AI for Good programme to predict daily solar generation at mobile network sites and plan how to use grid, solar, diesel and battery supply. Contents: three data sets: site basic information and grid outages (diesel generator output power, battery capacity, grid output power and planned outage hours), hourly solar power statistics with weather (direct normal, diffuse horizontal and global horizontal irradiance, among others) and energy output in kWh, and hourly energy consumption of the base stations. The challenge text notes that energy is on average over 90% of network costs and that diesel generators back up sites where grid supply is unstable. Producer: ITU AI for Good challenge on Zindi; the operator is not named on the pages read. Coverage: anonymised sites and days. Format and access: CSV files and a starter notebook downloaded from Zindi after creating a free account and joining the challenge. Licence: challenge data may be accessed, used and shared under CC BY-SA 4.0 according to the challenge rules. Caveats: site locations are not given, so outage plans cannot be tied to real grids. Simulation uses: energy supply scheduling and battery or diesel sizing for telecom sites, resilience of mobile networks to grid outages, and solar forecasting. Related records: data-itu-5g-base-station-energy-consumption-challenge and data-zindi-itu-beam-level-mobile-traffic-2880-beams-30-base-stations.
